meta.name: AI Sales Executive MVP
source_documents: PRD: AI Sales Executive MVP: Product Requirements (PRD), Google Doc
meta.reference_product: SaleAssist.ai (AIVA): first-line AI sales agent with Hot/Warm/Cold grading and human handoff
meta.goal: Reply to new leads within 5 minutes on WhatsApp, web chat and email, qualify and grade them, follow up silent leads on day 1, 3 and 7, and hand Hot leads to a human with a summary.
how_to_use: Give this file to Claude Code at the start of every session.
Build one day at a time using build_plan. Do not start the next day until the owner approves.
Where this file and a later chat decision disagree, the later decision wins and this file is updated.
Never hardcode secrets. All secrets come from environment variables.

decisions.use_case: Own company's sales, generic industry, buyers and clients only
decisions.launch_volume: Under 100 leads per month, tested by the owner only
decisions.customers: Global, English only, deals of any size, sales cycle 1 to 7 days
decisions.persona: Human-style first name and professional formal tone. Must state it is an AI if asked directly.
decisions.approval_policy: Fully automatic except quotations, which a human must approve before sending
decisions.after_human_takeover: AI drafts replies, human approves each one
decisions.model: Claude, called from the backend only

in_mvp: Channels: WhatsApp (test mode on owner's own number), website chat widget, email
Lead intake: website form webhook, CSV upload, manual entry, WhatsApp first message creates a lead
Knowledge base from pasted text and uploaded PDF or Word files
Price answers calculated from rules, with a fixed price list as the fallback
Follow-ups on day 1, day 3 and day 7
Human handoff with summary, assignment by manager, draft-and-approve after takeover
Dashboard: leads list, chat view, knowledge base manager, simple analytics
Hot lead alerts to the dashboard and to the salesperson on WhatsApp
Daily email report: new and Hot leads, leads stuck with no reply
Motion and animation: P1 items in motion_design (AI presence orb, streaming replies, grade and Hot alert transitions, handoff transition)
phase_2: Website crawl and Google Sheet import for the knowledge base
Manager chat (ask the AI about the pipeline)
Motion P2 and P3 items: pipeline flow ribbon, 3D lead constellation, scroll-driven marketing site
cut_order_if_late: 0. Motion polish (ship with plain CSS transitions)
2. Price rules engine, fall back to fixed price list
4. Document upload, keep pasted text only

model.note: Model id is an env variable so it can be changed without code changes.

conventions: UUID primary keys, created_at and updated_at on every table
Soft delete with deleted_at for leads and knowledge items
Row level security on every table, based on the role in profiles

price_rules.note: Formulas run in a safe expression evaluator in the backend, never by the model. The model only passes inputs (size, quantity) and receives the computed result.

keys: business_profile (name, what we sell, working hours, timezone)

webhook_events.note: Store every inbound webhook before processing. Unique event_id makes retries safe.

agent.design: One agent loop per inbound event: load lead and history, retrieve knowledge, call Claude with tools, run guardrail checks, then send, queue for approval, or hand off.
system_prompt_rules: You are {persona_name}, a sales executive for {business_name}. Write in a professional, formal tone, in English.
Keep replies to 3 or 4 lines. Ask at most one or two questions per message.
Use only facts from the retrieved knowledge and tool results. If the answer is not there, say you will check and call hand_off_to_human.
If the customer asks whether they are speaking to a bot or an AI, say clearly that you are an AI assistant for the company, and offer a human.
Collect, in a natural order: name and phone, requirement or product, budget, timeline and location. Save each answer with update_lead.
Never invent prices, discounts, stock or specifications. Prices come only from get_price.
Never promise delivery dates or lead times unless a knowledge item states them as standard. Otherwise say a team member will confirm.
Never offer or agree to a discount. Pass discount requests to a human.
Stay on topic about the business. Politely decline unrelated requests.
If the customer writes STOP, UNSUBSCRIBE or similar, call stop_contact and send one short confirmation.
If the customer asks for a person, is angry, or raises a complaint, call hand_off_to_human.

tools.name: get_price
tools.purpose: Compute a price from price_rules. Runs deterministic code, never the model.
tools.output: {unit_price, total, currency, rule_ids, breakdown} or {error: no_rule_matches}

tools.name: set_grade
tools.purpose: Set Hot, Warm or Cold with a reason and signals

tools.name: draft_quotation
tools.purpose: Create a quotation from price results. Never sent without human approval.

tools.name: book_meeting
tools.purpose: Record a meeting or call request and notify the assigned person. Calendar integration is phase 2.

tools.name: hand_off_to_human
tools.purpose: Create a handoff with summary and alert the salesperson

tools.name: stop_contact
tools.purpose: Mark the lead opted out and cancel follow-ups

hot_signals: Gave a budget and a timeline
Asked for a quote or price
Asked to talk to a person
rules: Hot: at least two hot signals, or an explicit request for a quote or a person.
Warm: has a clear requirement but is missing budget or timeline, or replies slowly.
Cold: no clear requirement, or no reply after the last follow-up.
grading.regrade: After every inbound message the agent may call set_grade. The reason is stored and shown in the dashboard.

followups.send_window: Business hours of the lead's timezone when known, otherwise the business timezone
followups.after_last_followup_without_reply: Set grade to cold and keep stage unchanged
followups.content: Short, formal, references the earlier conversation, one clear question. Generated by the agent using prompts/followup.md.

triggers: Agent does not know the answer
Quotation drafted (goes to approval queue, owner or manager notified)

summary_schema.chat_link: URL to the lead chat view in the dashboard

alerts: WhatsApp message to the assigned salesperson, or to the manager if unassigned
handoff.after_takeover: human_takeover = true. Agent switches to draft mode: it writes a draft reply, status pending_approval, and the human approves, edits or discards it.

pre_send_checks: No price or number in the reply that is not present in a get_price result or a retrieved knowledge chunk
No discount language: discount, offer, reduced, special price, unless quoting a stored rule
No delivery date promises: regex for dates and phrases such as 'will be delivered by'
Message length within 3 to 4 lines for WhatsApp and chat
No message if opted_out, quiet hours do not apply to direct replies but apply to follow-ups
guardrails.on_failure: Regenerate once with the failure reason. If it fails again, do not send: create a handoff with reason 'guardrail failure'.
guardrails.quote_rule: Any message with is_quote = true is created with status pending_approval and only sent after a manager or owner approves.

agent.first_reply_delay: Send within 5 minutes. Add a short random delay (for example 20 to 90 seconds) so replies feel natural, configurable in settings.
agent.context_window: Send the last 20 messages plus the lead record and top 5 knowledge chunks. Summarize older messages into a running summary stored on the conversation.

conventions: Success: {data, meta}. Error: {error: {code, message, fields, details}}
Auth: Supabase JWT in Authorization: Bearer for dashboard calls
Webhooks: verify provider signature, store event first, process idempotently

confidential_documents: Private storage bucket, no public URLs
Documents are read by the backend only for knowledge extraction
Do not send document contents to the model unless they are retrieved chunks for the current question
rules: Anthropic API key and all provider keys stay on the backend only
Row level security on all tables, tested
Rate limit public endpoints per IP and per session
Verify WhatsApp and email webhook signatures
Audit log for settings, role, price rule and knowledge changes, and every approval
Redact phone numbers and emails in application logs

opt_out: STOP reply on WhatsApp creates an opt-out and cancels follow-ups

environment_variables.note: Embedding provider is open: Claude does not provide an embeddings model, so choose one (for example Voyage AI or OpenAI embeddings) before Day 1 step 4.

rules: Work one day at a time. After each day, run the acceptance checks, summarize, and wait for owner approval.
Write tests with the code. Do not move on with failing tests.

backend: RLS: a sales user cannot read leads assigned to others
Webhook idempotency: same event id processed once
Opt-out: no outbound message is created for an opted-out lead
Follow-up skip rules for each skip reason
Price rules: fixed, per unit, tiered and formula cases, and rejection of unsafe formulas
Quotation messages never reach status queued without approval
Guardrails: unsupported price, discount wording, and delivery date wording are blocked
Grading: scripted conversations produce expected grades
agent_evaluation_set: 20 sample conversations covering: price question, unknown question, discount request, delivery date request, 'are you a bot', STOP, angry customer, off-topic request, vague requirement, ready-to-buy lead
Run on every prompt change and store the pass rate in ai_runs
end_to_end: New lead from form to first reply
Silent lead through all three follow-ups
Hot lead to human takeover to approved draft
Quotation draft to approval to send

motion_design.status: Added 21 Nov 2026. Visual reference: saleassist.ai. The page text does not expose its CSS or motion details, so this spec is original and built from the elements visible on that page: near-black theme (#0B0D10), LIVE badge, 'Speaking' status, 'Connected to a Human' status, live status panels, a carousel with a 1/4 indicator, a comparison of Chat 2% / Voice 3% / Video 27%, and removable filter tags. Nothing here copies their assets or code.
motion_design.intent: The product should feel alive: the AI is visibly listening, thinking, qualifying and handing over, instead of a plain list of chats. Motion explains state, it is never decoration.

dashboard: Framer Motion (React) for layout, presence and gestures
CSS variables and CSS animations for loops
Lottie (lottie-react) only for 2 or 3 pre-made loops
Canvas 2D for the orb particles, no heavy WebGL in the MVP
libraries.widget: Vanilla JS with Web Animations API and CSS only, target under 25 KB gzipped, no framework
avoid: GSAP ScrollTrigger in the MVP dashboard (marketing site only, phase 3)

visual_language.theme: Dark first. Background #0B0D10, surface #12151A, raised #181C23, hairline borders rgba(255,255,255,0.08)
visual_language.accent: A single electric accent #6EE7B7 for 'AI is active', used only for live states
visual_language.glow_rule: Glow is used only on live or Hot elements, so it keeps meaning
visual_language.type: Inter or Geist for UI, tabular numbers for all metrics

rules: Only animate transform and opacity, plus filter blur on small surfaces
One primary motion per screen at a time
Entrances use enter easing, exits are faster than entrances (about 60 percent of the duration)
Loops pause when the tab is hidden

signature_moments.where: Lead chat header, web widget header, sidebar 'AI status'
signature_moments.description: A small soft orb that represents the AI. States: idle (slow breathing scale 1 to 1.04 over 4s with faint accent glow), listening (ring pulses outward each time a customer message arrives), thinking (orb tightens, three orbiting particles rotate at 1.2s per turn), speaking (orb edge ripples in time with streamed tokens), paused (desaturated, no glow), human takeover (orb crossfades into the salesperson's avatar ring over 420ms).
signature_moments.implementation: CSS radial gradients and a 120 by 120 canvas for particles. State comes from a single aiState value: idle, listening, thinking, speaking, paused, human.
signature_moments.label: Text beside the orb changes with the state: 'Online', 'Reading', 'Thinking', 'Replying', 'Paused', 'Connected to a human'

signature_moments.description: Customer bubble slides up 12px with a soft spring. A typing indicator of three dots morphs from the orb for 400 to 900ms. The AI reply streams word by word with each word fading in from 0 to 1 opacity over 120ms and 2px blur to 0. When the reply finishes, the bubble settles with a 1px overshoot and the delivery tick animates (one tick draws in, then the second).
signature_moments.implementation: Server-Sent Events chunks are appended as spans with a CSS animation delay of 0. Respect reduced motion by showing text instantly.

signature_moments.where: Lead detail header and leads list rows
signature_moments.description: When the AI grades a lead, the grade badge morphs between colors over 420ms. For Cold to Warm, the badge cross-fades and grows 6 percent. For Hot, a ring expands once from the badge and fades (700ms), then a slow 2.4s glow pulse continues until the lead is acknowledged by a human. The reason text appears beneath the badge, typed in line by line with 40ms stagger.
signature_moments.implementation: Framer Motion layoutId on the badge so it animates between the list row and the detail header.

signature_moments.description: A toast slides in from the top right with a spring. It carries the lead name, grade badge and the one-line need. The toast has a thin progress line around its border that fills over 8 seconds as a countdown to auto-dismiss, but pauses on hover. The bell icon in the top bar rings once (rotate -12, 12, -6, 6, 0 over 600ms) and its counter ticks up with a vertical roll. Clicking the toast flies the lead row to the top of the list and highlights it with a 1.2s accent wash.
signature_moments.implementation: Framer Motion AnimatePresence for toasts, layout animation for the list reorder.

signature_moments.where: Lead detail when a human takes over
signature_moments.description: The handoff summary card unfolds from the grade badge (scale from 0.92, opacity 0 to 1, 420ms). Fields fill in one by one: need, budget, timeline, next step, each with a tiny check that draws itself. The orb crossfades to the salesperson's avatar ring and the chat composer changes from a locked 'AI is replying' bar to an editable composer with a slide-up. A 'Connected to a human' status chip appears with a soft pulse.
signature_moments.implementation: Sequence with Framer Motion variants and staggerChildren 80ms.

signature_moments.description: Day 1, Day 3 and Day 7 are dots on a vertical line. The current step's dot pulses. When a follow-up is sent, the dot fills with accent color and a short line draws to the next dot (320ms). If skipped because the lead replied, the dot turns into a check and the remaining dots fade to 40 percent.

Each pending quotation is a card with a subtle shimmer on its border. Approve slides the card to the right and replaces it with a small 'Sent' stamp that scales from 1.3 to 1 with a haptic-style bounce; reject slides left and fades. Totals count up from 0 over 600ms with tabular numbers. The next card moves up with a layout animation.
signature_moments.implementation: Framer Motion drag with threshold, buttons as the accessible path.

signature_moments.description: A horizontal ribbon shows New, Qualifying, Qualified, Quote sent, Booked, Won. Small particles flow along the ribbon, their count proportional to lead volume per stage. Hot leads are brighter particles. Hovering a stage slows the flow and lifts its card. Numbers count up when the screen first enters view.
signature_moments.implementation: Canvas 2D, capped at 200 particles, pauses when off screen.

signature_moments.description: Reply-time and conversion by channel (WhatsApp, web chat, email) as bars that grow from the baseline with 40ms stagger and spring_soft. Hover shows a tooltip that follows the cursor with 80ms lag.
signature_moments.implementation: SVG bars, no chart library animation conflicts.

signature_moments.description: The closed bubble has a slow breathing ring (3.2s). On click it expands from the bubble into the chat panel: a circle morph to a rounded rectangle over 420ms with spring_soft, content fades in 120ms later. The header shows the orb and a LIVE badge with a tiny blinking dot. The first AI message arrives after the typing indicator. A 'Connected to a human' state replaces the orb with the person's initials ring.
signature_moments.implementation: Web Animations API, transform-origin at the bubble position, honors prefers-reduced-motion.

signature_moments.description: After a paste or upload, the text visibly splits into chunk cards that fly into a stack (stagger 30ms) and each gets a small spark when its embedding is saved. A progress ring around the item shows chunks done. Test search shows retrieved chunks lighting up in order of relevance with a score bar that grows.
signature_moments.implementation: Framer Motion layout and variants, progress from the embed_knowledge job status.

signature_moments.description: A compact strip shows 'AI active', average first-reply time in seconds, and leads waiting. The first-reply number ticks with a vertical roll when it changes. A tiny sparkline of the last 24 hours draws left to right on load. A small 'Live' dot blinks once every 3 seconds.
signature_moments.implementation: Supabase realtime subscriptions drive the values.

optional_marketing_page_phase_3.note: Only after the MVP works. Inspired by the reference page's structure: headline, persona cards with 'Speaking' status, a channel comparison and a touchpoints carousel.
ideas: Hero headline with word-by-word reveal and a live demo chat running beside it
Persona cards that switch between 'Listening' and 'Speaking' on scroll
Scroll-driven lead journey: a lead dot travels from form to WhatsApp reply to Hot handoff

accessibility_and_performance.reduced_motion: When prefers-reduced-motion is set: no loops, no particles, no parallax, transitions become 120ms opacity fades, streamed text appears instantly. Keep a manual 'Reduce motion' switch in Settings.
accessibility_and_performance.focus: Motion never moves focus. Toasts are announced with aria-live polite, Hot alerts with aria-live assertive.
performance_budget: 60 fps on a mid-range Android phone
Canvas animations stop when the tab is hidden or the element is off screen
Total JS added for motion in the dashboard under 60 KB gzipped
accessibility_and_performance.no_flashing: No element flashes more than 3 times per second

build_notes.day_3_slot: Motion is a polish step at the end of Day 3. Build P1 items only if the Day 3 acceptance checks already pass. If not, ship with CSS transitions and add motion after launch.
build_notes.single_source_of_truth: All durations, easings and colors live in dashboard/src/styles/motion.ts and CSS variables. No hardcoded timings in components.
testing: Storybook or a /motion test page showing every component in each state
Check on a throttled CPU (4x slowdown) in browser dev tools
